# Vanishing buffer scales: source stratification and original-volume splitting

This is a conditional limit theorem for actual attained bad pairs with the
full-space logarithmic parameter. It bounds the PHYSICAL parameter
h_e=epsilon^(d+1)L_e, localizes all deepest marks uniformly inside their own
fibers, and splits the actual original-volume allocations into zero and
positive limiting classes. Exact deepest-mark rigidity gives disjoint source
parity budgets and, more strongly, excludes every mixed integer anchored
combination. A bounded touching-plane replacement then upgrades the sampled
limit to uniform convergence to a finite-PL function. These conclusions do
not give a Gamma payment for either class.

the contributor proposed the scaling and the original-volume splitting. The proof below
retains the crucial correction that the zero-fiber set need not itself be a
face. A zero source uses its OWN minimal containing base face.

## 1. Standing hypotheses and actual normalization

Fix d>=1, N=d+1 and a finite lattice-complete canonical base
P=conv(P) intersect Lambda, with k occupied parities. Consider epsilon_j down
to zero and actual compatible positive convex fibers K_(j,z), z in P, with
canonical hulls C_j. Work in the fixed relative ambient space
aff(P) x R^d. Assume the normalized body compactness already established for
the original bad sublevel: after a subsequence,

    K_(j,z) -> K_z in Hausdorff distance,   V_z=|K_z|>0,
    M_j=sum_z |K_(j,z)| -> M>0,

and all fibers are uniformly bounded and contain common interior balls on
each fixed base. Their within-fiber covariance matrices Sigma_j converge to
a positive definite Sigma. Thus Gamma_j(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma_j u) is uniformly
comparable to the Euclidean norm.

Assume every nonempty proper closed minor T of P satisfies at the limit

    V(T)<=k(T) M/k.                                      (1)

The strict original bad-minor quotas imply (1), but strictness is not needed
inside this note. A closed minor means P intersect conv(T)=T; k(T) is the
inherited occupied-parity count, equivalently the restriction of the parity
classes of Lambda.

Let L_j be positive continuous concave on C_j, logarithmically normalized by

    (1/M_j) integral_(S_j) log L_j dm_j=0.               (2)

The actual invariant buffered cap at w=(p,y) has displacement

    epsilon_j [L_j(w) E_(K_(j,p))(y)/M_j]^(1/N) Gamma_j(u)
       =[h_j(w) E_(K_(j,p))(y)/M_j]^(1/N) Gamma_j(u),
    h_j=epsilon_j^N L_j.                               (3)

All pure-base closed halfspaces are included unchanged. Write Q_j for the
maximum raw buffered depth, and assume a common strict sublevel

    Q_j/M_j <= b < 1/k.                                (4)

The intended bad-minimum setting has the stronger b<Gamma_d/k. The present
bounded argument uses only (1), (4), and the explicitly stated deepest-source
and martingale properties below; it does not infer joint minimality from them.

Let J_j be ALL strict-base-gap deepest bases, those with baseDepth_j(p)>Q_j.
At each p in J_j there is one proper deepest mark Y_(j,p). Pass to a subsequence
on which J_j=J is constant. Assume J is nonempty, as supplied at attained bad
minima by the actual atomic cleanup theorem. Suppose there are nonnegative
weights sigma_(j,p), p in J, summing to one, and, for each positive weight,
probability rows rho_(j,p), such that

    E_(rho_(j,p)) w=Y_(j,p),
    E_(rho_(j,p)) L_j=L_j(Y_(j,p)),
    sum_(p in J) [sigma_(j,p)/L_j(Y_(j,p))] rho_(j,p)
                                      =dm_j/(M_j L_j). (5)

Zero-weight rows may be omitted; their arbitrary later choice is irrelevant.
These are the already proved exact parameter-stationarity contact rows, not
physical surface rows. Finite-PL representatives are permitted but no bound
on their plane slopes is assumed or needed.

## 2. Uniform boundedness of the physical parameter

There is a finite constant B such that

    max_(z in P, X in K_(j,z)) h_j(z,X) <= B           (6)

for all j. Here is the compactness contradiction proof, which does not hold
epsilon fixed.

Put m_(j,z)=max_(K_(j,z)) h_j(z,.). Actual compatibility and concavity make
the finite array m_j sampled-concave: choose maximizing inputs in any anchored
representation and form their actual convex combination in the target fiber.
If A_j=max_z m_(j,z) tended to infinity, pass to a limit

    a_(j,z)=m_(j,z)/A_j -> a_z>=0,    max_z a_z=1.

The array a is nonnegative sampled-concave and nonzero. The positive-set
occupied-parity theorem in Section 3 of
`candidate 27d482de82ed9f88`, applied to
the limiting masses and (1), gives a fixed p with a_p>0 and

    baseDepth(p)>=M/k.                                (7)

For completeness, that arithmetic theorem covers the positive set of a by
closed caps of mass <M/k if (7) fails. Maximal thresholds give r witnesses
with distinct parities disjoint from a surviving closed minor T inside {a=0}.
Midpoint positivity of a gives both disjointness statements. The resulting
r+k(T)<=k and covering mass imply V(T)>k(T)M/k, contradicting (1). It does
not assume {a=0} is a face or a closed minor.

Let g_(j,p) be the ordinary centroid of K_(j,p). A nonnegative concave
function on a d-body has value at its centroid at least its maximum/(d+1):
homothety from a maximizing point gives integral h>=max(h)|K|/(d+1), and
Jensen gives the centroid inequality. Consequently

    h_j(p,g_(j,p))>=m_(j,p)/N -> infinity.

At that point projective energy is |K_(j,p)|, bounded below. The physical
buffer in (3), for Euclidean unit u, therefore tends uniformly to infinity.
Once it exceeds the common continuous diameter, every fiber with nonnegative
base drift from p is wholly captured by EVERY such buffered cap. Those bases
form a containing closed pure-base halfspace. Pure-base cuts themselves are
allowed, so the buffered depth at this centroid equals baseDepth_j(p).
Base depths depend continuously on the finitely many volumes, because only
finitely many halfspace traces occur. Equation (7) contradicts (4). This
proves (6).

This proof bounds h_j, not L_j. It does not imply that the physical buffers
in (3) tend to zero.

## 3. A sampled concave limit and a nonempty zero-fiber set

Use the canonical concave-roof representative from the sampled hypographs,
which leaves all sampled values unchanged. Equation (6) also bounds this
representative on C_j. Bounded concave functions are equi-Lipschitz on common
compact fiber interiors. A diagonal subsequence therefore gives local uniform
limits h_z on int K_z. Each is nonnegative concave and either strictly positive
there or identically zero. Take its upper-semicontinuous concave boundary
closure. Anchored inequalities pass first through interior input points and
then by closure; the canonical sampled roof gives a nonnegative jointly
concave representative h on C=conv(S). This is the same compactness argument
as Section 4 of
`candidate f17e4f2b0ba9ee84`,
now allowing entire sampled fibers to vanish.

Define

    Z={z in P:h_z is identically zero in int K_z},
    U=P outside Z.                                    (8)

On z in Z the convergence is actually uniform on the WHOLE moving fiber:

    max_(K_(j,z)) h_j ->0.                            (9)

Indeed fix g_z in int K_z and a common inner ball of radius r. If R bounds
the distance of every current point from g_z, positivity and concavity give
max h_j<=(1+R/r)h_j(z,g_z), by the opposite-inner-ball-point argument. The
right side tends to zero. No unbounded boundary spike is possible for a
bounded nonnegative concave function with an interior value tending to zero.

The set Z is NONEMPTY. Otherwise every fiber has a fixed positive limiting
interior value and hence its maximum m_(j,z) is uniformly bounded below.
For a nonnegative concave function with maximum m on a d-body, homothety
superlevel integration gives

    average log h >= log m-H_d,
    H_d=1+1/2+...+1/d.

Thus the mixed average of log h_j would be bounded below. But (2) says exactly

    (1/M_j) integral log h_j dm_j=N log epsilon_j -> -infinity.

This contradiction proves the assertion. The possibility Z=P, equivalently
h=0 on every sampled fiber, remains allowed.

The zero set need not be convex or be one face. What is true is the following
precise statement. If p in Z and F_p is the minimal face of conv(P) containing
p, then

    P intersect F_p subset Z.                        (10)

For every z in P intersect F_p, p is a convex combination with a positive
coefficient of z and other points of F_p: continue the ray from z through the
relative-interior point p to the opposite boundary of F_p. If h were positive
at an interior point of the z-fiber, choose interior points in all other input
fibers in that representation. Their combination is interior to K_p, because
the positive input weights combine actual small balls. Sampled concavity and
nonnegativity would make h positive there, contradicting p in Z. Thus z is
in Z. In rank zero F_p is the whole singleton.

## 4. Deepest marks stay uniformly inside their own fibers

All actual deepest marks, and in particular Y_(j,p), lie in a uniform own-fiber
interior core. Two points make this conclusion independent of any claimed
uniform proper-cap gap.

First Q_j has a positive lower bound. At the center of one common inner ball,
every containing ambient cap with nonzero continuous normal captures at least
half that ball; the nonnegative buffer only increases capture. A pure-base
cap contains the entire own fiber. Thus one fixed positive half-ball volume
is a lower bound on the maximum raw depth.

Second a sampled boundary point Y=(p,y), y in boundary K_p, has ordinary raw
depth zero. Choose a continuous supporting normal u!=0 of K_p at y. The finite
array H_z=h_(K_z)(u) is sampled-concave by actual inclusion. Its finite support
LP gives a base slope a with H_z<=H_p+a.(z-p). Hence

    u.X-a.(z-p)<=H_p

supports the entire canonical hull and touches at Y. Its outer closed cap has
zero mixed volume, because its nonzero continuous normal has at most a
(d-1)-dimensional trace in each positive d-fiber.

If deepest marks approached such a boundary point, marked-energy boundary
continuity and (6) would make their physical displacement in (3) tend to zero.
Test the fixed limiting support normal/tilt just constructed at these marks.
Its thresholds converge to the support value, and the current projected laws
converge to the old absolutely continuous projected law. The captured mass
therefore tends to zero, contradicting the positive lower bound on Q_j.
Finiteness of P and compactness now give a uniform own-interior distance.

Pass to a subsequence so every Y_(j,p) converges to an interior Y_p=(p,y_p).
Local uniform convergence gives

    h_(j,p):=h_j(Y_(j,p)) -> h_p:=h(Y_p),
    h_p=0 iff p in Z.                                 (11)

Also the physical sampled buffers converge uniformly, with zero boundary
extensions, to [h E/M]^(1/N) Gamma. On interior cores this follows from local
uniform h convergence and energy continuity; on boundary collars it follows
from (6) and energy vanishing. The standard all-normal slab comparison,
including unchanged pure-base traces, therefore gives convergence of Q_j to
the maximum depth Q of this limiting possibly degenerate buffer. Every Y_p
is a limiting deepest mark. On Z its buffer is zero, so its depth is the
ORIGINAL unbuffered depth Q. No strict base gap at the limit is asserted.

### 4a. A bounded finite-plane representative and uniform boundary convergence

There is a stronger regularity conclusion AFTER the source-interiority proof.
It is not an assumption about the original changing PL planes. At every
Y_(j,p), p in J, choose a continuous-coordinate supergradient c_(j,p) of h_j.
The uniform own-source inner ball and (6) give a uniform bound on these
gradients. Use the finite sampled touching-plane construction and its
minimum-norm base slope bound from
`candidate 87de5b3c068291f1`.
It supplies affine A_(j,p) with uniformly bounded FULL coefficients such that

    A_(j,p)>=h_j on S_j,        A_(j,p)(Y_(j,p))=h_(j,p).

The finite minimum V_j=min_(p in J) A_(j,p) is positive on C_j, majorizes h_j
on S_j, and touches every positive certificate source. The global certificate
applied to V_j/epsilon_j^N and L_j gives

    0>= (1/M_j) integral_(S_j) log(V_j/h_j) dm_j>=0.

Hence V_j=h_j on EVERY sampled fiber, including its boundary. Replacing the
unsampled extension by V_j preserves the actual parameter, normalization,
depths, and every row equality (5). In particular the replacement is also an
attained minimizing representative when the initial pair was one.

After a further subsequence, each of these at most |J| bounded plane arrays
converges. Its minimum converges uniformly on every common bounded ambient
set to a finite-PL concave h. This h is nonnegative on C and agrees with the
previous interior limit. Thus, using the plane extension at moving points,

    sup_(z in P, X in K_(j,z)) |h_j(z,X)-h(z,X)| ->0.    (11a)

The extension h may have a small negative value just outside C; (11a) is
an ambient comparison and does not assert positivity of that extension on a
fixed neighborhood. Its restrictions to the LIMITING fibers are nonnegative.

This proves uniform sampled-boundary convergence for the physical h_j at
these certified minima, unlike arbitrary nearly optimizing concave weights.
It does not give a positive limiting parameter or bounded slopes for L_j
itself, whose coefficients divide by epsilon_j^N.

If p in J has h_p=0, its own selected limiting plane has continuous gradient
zero. Indeed positivity on a uniform source ball gives the sharper bound
||c_(j,p)||<=h_(j,p)/r; equation (11) makes this tend to zero. The limiting
plane is therefore base-affine, nonnegative on conv(P), and zero at p. If h
is not identically zero, that plane cannot be identically zero. Its zero set
is a proper exposed base face G_p containing the minimal face F_p, and

    P intersect G_p subset Z.                         (11b)

Together with the original-volume cover (16a) below, this also gives

    Z=P intersect union_(p in J intersect Z, sigma_p>0) G_p

in the nontrivial case. The finite face cover carries no asserted efficient
sum of parity counts.

## 5. Exact original-volume rows and their limiting block structure

Define the ORIGINAL-volume row measures

    d eta_(j,p)=[sigma_(j,p) L_j/L_j(Y_(j,p))] d rho_(j,p)
              =[sigma_(j,p) h_j/h_(j,p)] d rho_(j,p).

For zero sigma use the zero measure. Equations (5) give exactly

    eta_(j,p)(S_j)=sigma_(j,p),
    sum_p eta_(j,p)=dm_j/M_j,
    eta_(j,p)<=dm_j/M_j.                              (12)

After a subsequence sigma_(j,p)->sigma_p and these finite measures converge
weakly (or their bounded original-volume densities converge weak-star on a
common bounded fiber domain) to eta_p, with

    eta_p(S)=sigma_p,       sum_p eta_p=dm/M.           (13)

All limiting rows are absolutely continuous with respect to original mixed
volume. A row with sigma_p=0 disappears and is not assigned a fictitious
conditional probability.

If p in U, then h_p>0. Equation (9) gives the exact estimate

    eta_(j,p)(fibers over Z)
       <=[sigma_(j,p)/h_(j,p)] max_(z in Z) max_(K_(j,z)) h_j
       ->0.                                           (14)

Thus eta_p allocates no ORIGINAL volume to Z. This can also be viewed as the
inverse-h Fatou constraint; the displayed estimate avoids any exchange of
varying densities with a singular reciprocal limit.

If p in Z, its original row is supported on F_p already for EVERY j.
Indeed rho_(j,p) has base mean p and is supported in conv(P). Each supporting
functional exposing F_p is nonnegative after subtracting its value at p;
its expectation is zero. Hence the row is supported in that face. Positive
reweighting by h_j does not change base support. By (10),

    eta_(j,p)(fibers over U)=0 for every j,
    eta_p is supported over P intersect F_p subset Z.  (15)

Equations (13)--(15) yield the exact mass splitting

    sum_(p in J intersect Z) sigma_p=V(Z)/M,
    sum_(p in J intersect U) sigma_p=V(U)/M,            (16)

and the corresponding row sums equal the restricted ORIGINAL volume measures.
If both Z and U are nonempty, both limiting classes carry positive total
sigma mass. In particular there are positive-weight sources in each class.

There is also an exact finite geometric cover, with NO claimed efficient parity
cost:

    Z=P intersect union_(p in J intersect Z, sigma_p>0) F_p.   (16a)

The inclusion from right to left is (10). Every z in Z has positive target
volume in (13), so some surviving zero-class row allocates positive mass to
that fiber; (15) places z in its F_p. If U is nonempty all faces in (16a) are
proper, since a source in the relative interior of conv(P) would force h to
vanish on every sampled fiber. Neither disjointness of these faces nor a bound
on the sum of their individual parity counts has been proved here.

The original-volume rows eta_p/sigma_p are NOT claimed to be martingales.
Their finite-j versions already have the known covariance mean defect. Nor
do (14)--(15) forbid a positive source's TILTED probability row rho_(j,p)
from retaining a limiting mass on Z with zero original-volume weight. The
limiting reciprocal-h target can diverge there. The theorem deliberately
splits (12), not an unjustified finite limiting inverse-h transport.

### 5a. All original deepest bases of the limiting body lie in Z

There is a useful exact sharpening. Let Q_ordinary be the original unbuffered
maximum raw depth of the limiting family. Then

    Q_ordinary=Q,   and every original deepest base belongs to Z. (16b)

Since Z is nonempty and every limiting fiber has positive volume, (16) supplies
a source p in Z with sigma_p>0. Section 4 gives an actual interior limiting
mark Y_p with zero physical buffer and raw depth Q. Hence Q_ordinary>=Q.
Conversely nonnegative buffering gives original depth <= limiting buffered
depth at every mark, and the latter has maximum Q. This proves equality.

For the second assertion first note a general finite-family bound, valid at
any mark Y=(p,y):

    ordinaryDepth(Y)<=baseDepth(p)-|K_p|/2.             (16c)

Choose a minimizing closed pure-base cap, tightened to pass through p. Write
it as {a.(z-p)>=0}; in rank zero take a=0. At sufficiently large finite base
tilt, the two ambient caps with normals (T a,u) and (T a,-u), through Y,
capture every strictly positive base fiber fully, every strictly negative
one not at all, and complementary continuous parts on the zero-base trace.
Here u!=0 is arbitrary; bounded fibers make the strict statuses exact for
large T. Their raw masses sum to

    2 baseDepth(p)-V{z:a.(z-p)=0}
       <=2 baseDepth(p)-|K_p|.

Continuous hyperplane boundaries have zero d-volume in every sampled fiber,
so the closed-cap convention adds no term. At least one of the two caps has
mass at most the stated average, proving (16c).

At an interior mark a strictly positive scalar physical buffer therefore
strictly increases depth above its original value. If the new value reaches
baseDepth, (16c) proves strictness. Otherwise proper-gap attainment gives an
own-proper minimizing buffered cap; removing its positive displacement
strictly removes own-fiber volume, proving that its new mass exceeds original
depth. This is the same exact proper-own-strip strictness used in the global
parameter certificate, with no regularity at other fibers required.

An original deepest mark has positive depth Q and hence is own-interior. If
its base were in U, h would be strictly positive there, and its physical
buffer would be positive. Strictness would make its limiting buffered depth
larger than Q, contradiction. Thus its base lies in Z. This conclusion does
not identify every point of Z as deepest, and does not make Z a closed minor.

## 6. Deepest rigidity excludes mixed integer anchored combinations

Put J_0=J intersect Z and J_+=J intersect U, including zero-limit-weight
proper sources. There is no integer anchored representation

    r=sum_(p in J) lambda_p p in P,  lambda_p>=0, sum lambda_p=1,

whose positive inputs meet BOTH J_0 and J_+.              (17)

Here is the exact finite-j argument. Form Y_j=sum lambda_p Y_(j,p). Convexity
of the buffered Q_j-superlevel makes Y_j deepest. Its base r is still strict
base-gap: every closed pure-base halfspace containing r contains at least
one positively weighted input, and its mass is therefore >Q_j. Thus Y_j is
an own-proper deepest mark and an attained active cap exists there.

Normalize its continuous normal by Gamma_j(u)=1. Proper own capture makes
its threshold the exact upper Q_j-quantile c_j. Every input deepest mark
satisfies

    N_cap.Y_(j,p)-epsilon_j f_j(Y_(j,p))<=c_j,

while equality holds at Y_j. Averaging these inequalities and using concavity
of f_j forces equality throughout. With F_j=E_j^(1/d),

    f_j=M_j^(-1/N) L_j^(1/N) F_j^(d/N).

Strict monotonicity and the equality case of the positive weighted geometric
mean force equality in BOTH concavity inequalities and proportionality:

    L_j(Y_(j,p))/F_j(Y_(j,p)) is independent of every positive input p.
                                                               (18)

The equality theorem for joint E^(1/d) concavity then makes the marked input
fibers positive homothetic copies, with scale proportional to F_j. (This uses
the proved strict inclusion step as well as the marked equality theorem in
`candidate 5811f0ad1132ce56`.) In
particular, for any two positive inputs p,q,

    h_(j,p)/h_(j,q)
       =F_j(Y_(j,p))/F_j(Y_(j,q))
       =[|K_(j,p)|/|K_(j,q)|]^(1/d).                  (19)

Uniform positive volume bounds keep this ratio bounded above and away from
zero. Equation (11) therefore prevents one limiting value from being zero
and the other positive, proving (17). The energy bounds at uniform interior
marks would also suffice; (19) records the sharper exact geometric relation.

Each nonempty J_0 and J_+ is a closed minor. For an integer combination of
one class, the preceding finite-j argument puts r back in the SAME constant
set J and identifies its deepest mark with Y_j. Equality of L values at the
combination, followed by the interior limit, keeps r in that class. Thus

    P intersect conv(J_0)=J_0,    P intersect conv(J_+)=J_+.

In particular same-parity inputs from the two classes would have an actual
integer midpoint, violating (17). Hence

    k(J_0)+k(J_+)<=k(J)<=k(P).                         (20)

The same inequality holds after discarding zero-sigma sources. No target
parity partition is claimed: (20) concerns actual deepest SOURCE bases.

## 7. Calibrations and the remaining limitation

The entire-zero alternative h=0 is possible as a normalization limit:
fixed L=1 gives h_j=epsilon_j^N on any fixed family. The theorem is then a
single zero-class statement, not a forced nontrivial decomposition.

For the fact that Z need not be one face, take P={-1,0,1}, all fibers [-1,1],
and the positive base-concave roof with sampled values

    L_e(-1)=L_e(1)=e,       L_e(0)=e^(-2),  0<e<1.

With d=1 and equal volumes it is logarithmically normalized. Setting
epsilon=e gives h_e=(e^3,1,e^3), so Z={-1,1}, a union of two faces which is
not itself convex or closed. Uniform same-fiber rows, one at each fiber
centroid with sigma=1/3, satisfy (5) exactly and give the block split (16).
This is a geometric/measure calibration only: those three marks are NOT
asserted simultaneously deepest, and this product family does not satisfy
the bad sublevel (4). It checks the distinction between a global zero face
and the valid individual minimal-face statement.

The new decomposition keeps both actual original mass and an exact source
parity budget. Nevertheless target portions need not supply a compatible
convex family paid at Gamma_d per source parity, and parameter rows need not
be uniform fibers. The already proved one-gradient class-payment obstruction
prevents such an inference from transport alone. Joint body minimality and
the actual cap geometry would have to provide any additional payment.
This note supplies neither that payment nor an OC conclusion.

Subsequent strengthening: when the sequence globally optimizes the JOINT
body/parameter values (or is o(1)-optimal) in the established minimal-bad-base
compactness framework, the separate actual body argument in
`candidate cebc39c4f5ccbc96`
forces h=0 and Z=P. The present two-class theorem remains a valid structural
intermediate statement under its explicit weaker hypotheses; it is not a
claim that a nontrivial escape class survives that additional body argument.

passes 663 exact calibration checks: logarithmic normalization, actual
original/tilted row densities, all five proper closed-minor quotas of the
interval calibration, its failure of simultaneous deepestness, and the exact
homothety scale relation. These checks do not replace the analytic limit proof.
